passages.note: Third Reading vote shows Finchem voting Yea on SB1057, whose engrossed text is ballot-paper antifraud certification, not voter ID.

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding any other statute, any vendor that provides fraud countermeasures that are contained in and on the paper used for ballots shall be ISO 27001 certified, ISO 17025 certified or ISO 9001:2015 certified.
passages.note: Operative text sets ballot-paper vendor certification and anti-counterfeiting features; it states no voter-identity or eligibility verification rule.
Bill Status page lists Finchem as prime sponsor of SB1057, later vetoed by the Governor on 06/19/2026.

rows.reasoning: Finchem prime-sponsored and voted Yea on SB 1057 (2026), whose operative text certifies ballot-paper vendors and mandates anti-counterfeiting features (watermarks, holograms, ISO certification); it does not address 'How should the government verify a voter's identity and eligibility', so it establishes no rung. All three passages are adjacent — same broad election-integrity area, but not the ID-verification dimension the rungs order.
